=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For non-Bash file tools (Edit, Write, etc.), `family_label` is set to `record_shape(record)` which returns `f"{parent}/*"` where `parent` comes from the file path. A Linux directory name can contain backticks or newlines. The label and shape are interpolated into inline backtick-fenced Markdown without escaping: `` `{pattern['family_label']}` `` on line 674 and 701, and `` `{pattern['shape'] or pattern['tool_name']}` `` on line 703. A path containing backticks would close the inline code span and inject raw text into the Markdown body of an `ai:permission-prompt` issue consumed by the Claude issue implementer.
  WHY: An untrusted file path with backticks in a directory name (e.g. `/tmp/\`injected\`/file.py`) would produce `family_label = "/tmp/\`injected\`/*"`, which in inline code becomes `` `/tmp/\`injected\`/*` ``. The Markdown renderer would see a code span ending at the first backtick, then plain text `injected`, then a new code span `/*`. The injected text could contain misleading issue-prose formatting consumed by the downstream Clarify/Implement pipeline.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After processing `timeout` options and duration, the function does not skip a `--` end-of-options marker. GNU timeout accepts `timeout 5 -- git fetch` where `--` separates timeout options from the command. The remaining words `['--', 'git', 'fetch']` are passed to `_family_word`, which treats `--` as the first word and returns family word `-- git` instead of `git fetch`.
  WHY: `timeout 5 -- git fetch` and `timeout 5 git fetch` receive different families (`-- git` vs `git fetch`), so the former is filed separately from the latter, creating a spurious family issue for a well-formed invocation.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function detects `$(` outside single quotes but does not skip shell comments (`#` to end-of-line). A command such as `curl https://host # $(date)` has `$(date)` inside a shell comment where it never executes, but the detector returns True and assigns the `subst` construct to the family.
  WHY: The `_has_command_substitution` function is called on the `stripped` text (line 516). For `curl https://host # $(date)`, the text after heredoc removal is exactly that command. The `$(` inside the comment is detected, adding `subst` to constructs. The family becomes `('curl', ('subst',))` instead of `('curl', ())`, so this occurrence is filed under a different family than other `curl` invocations. The `_has_command_substitution` function was not updated to mirror the comment-handling that `_substitution_end` already received in review round 3 (lines 343–356).
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _family_core advances past timeout options and the duration argument, but does not skip a trailing '--' option terminator. For standard commands structured as timeout <duration> -- <command> (for example, timeout 5 -- git fetch), the '--' token remains at the head of the core command words. In _family_word, '--' is not recognized as a subcommand tool or script, so it is returned as the command word itself.
  WHY: Commands invoked using timeout <duration> -- <command> are assigned to a spurious family labeled '--' instead of their actual command family (such as git fetch), causing repeated permission prompt reports for those commands to be filed under a separate '--' family issue instead of grouping with their intended family.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _has_command_substitution scans for unquoted $( occurrences without checking for shell comments beginning with #. If a command contains an unquoted trailing comment that happens to mention a command substitution (for example, curl https://example.com # $(date)), the function returns True.
  WHY: The command is classified into the ... + subst family construct even though no runtime command substitution occurs in the command being executed. This causes the report to diverge from the main command family issue into a separate + subst family.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `pattern['shape']` and `pattern['family_label']` are interpolated into inline Markdown code spans (single backticks) without any escaping. The pre-existing `**Pattern:**` line had the same property, but the PR amplifies it: `issue_body` adds a `**Family:**` line and `family_comment_body` adds three more inline-code interpolations of `pattern['family_label']`, `pattern['shape']`, and `pattern['signature']`. A script basename that contains a backtick (e.g. `foo\`bar.py` survives as a positional in `_segment_shape`) or a first line of an unparseable command that contains a backtick will close the inline code span and the rest of the rendered Markdown — the body of an `ai:permission-prompt` issue — becomes attacker-controlled Markdown.
  WHY: A user-typed command such as `` python3 path/with/`backtick.py`` yields shape `python3 path/with/`backtick.py`, which renders as ``python3 path/with/`` then the `backtick.py` text is rendered as Markdown outside the inline code. Inside an issue body that the Claude issue implementer reads, this can mislead the implementer (e.g. a line that looks like a heading or a link). The pre-existing line had the same property, but the PR doubles the surface for it. A small defence (`shape.replace('`', '\\`')` before interpolation, or rendering these as a fenced code block) closes it.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: After the `timeout` option loop and the duration check, the function does not skip a `--` end-of-options marker. GNU `timeout` accepts `timeout 5 -- git fetch` where `--` separates timeout's options from the actual command. The current loop stops as soon as it sees a non-flag token and the duration regex consumes `5`, leaving `['--', 'git', 'fetch']` as `core`. `_family_word` then calls `_segment_shape` on that list; `_drop_global_value_options` keeps `--` unchanged (it is not a key in `_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS`), and `_segment_shape` treats `--` as the leading command, producing shape `['--', '*']` and a family word of `--` (or `-- git` depending on shape contents). The result is a spurious `--` family that is filed as a new `ai:permission-prompt` issue every time this valid `timeout 5 -- cmd` form is logged.
  WHY: a real, well-formed `timeout 5 -- git fetch` produces family `(--, ())` rather than `git fetch`; the well-formed cousin `timeout 5 git fetch` correctly resolves to `git fetch`. The test suite covers `timeout -k 5 git fetch`, `timeout $T git fetch`, and `timeout 1.5m git fetch` but not the `--` form, so the test would not catch this.
